area: third_party/veremi-nextgen submodule: what VeReMi-NextGen is, how it was generated, its realism content, and current/possible integration with SCMS-Simulator
current_state:
WHAT IT IS: VeReMi-NextGen is the successor of VeReMi/VeReMi-Extension — a misbehavior-detection (MBD) dataset + full dataset GENERATOR for V2X CAMs, by Hermann/Remmers/Eisermann/Erb/Kargl (Ulm Univ., vs-uulm), to appear IEEE VNC 2026 (third_party/veremi-nextgen/README.md:16-28). Submodule origin https://github.com/VeReMi-dataset/VeReMi-NextGen, pinned at single squashed commit acda994 "add scenarios" (.gitmodules; git log). Dataset itself is NOT vendored — Dataset/ is 20KB of Zenodo download links (record 19665762) for 4 subsets x 15 attacks + ground-truth JSONs (Dataset/readme.md). Generator/ is ~16GB: a full vendored MOSAIC 25.0 installation (Generator/simulation/mosaic/lib/mosaic/*-25.0.jar), 8 ready-to-run scenarios in both Generator/docker/scenarios/ and Generator/simulation/mosaic/scenarios/, CamApp Java source, attack injector, CaTCH MBD system, Optuna param optimization.

GENERATION STACK (NOT Artery/Veins): Eclipse MOSAIC 25.2 + SUMO 1.25.0 + OMNeT++ 6.1 + INET 4.5.4 via MOSAIC's omnetpp-federate (README.md:6-9 badges; Generator/docker/Dockerfile ARG MOSAIC_VERSION=25.2; bin/fed/omnetpp installer). Federates: Application+OMNeT+SUMO+Output on; cell/sns/ns3 off (Documentation/Eclipse MOSAIC/Config/README.md:7-18).

RADIO MODEL (Documentation/Eclipse MOSAIC/Config/README.md:175-239 and Generator/docker/scenarios/*/omnetpp/omnetpp.ini): IEEE 802.11p/ITS-G5, 5.9 GHz, channel 4, 10 MHz BW, 6 Mbps, tx power 0.02 W, sensitivity -81 dBm, SNIR threshold 4 dB, background+thermal noise -110 dBm, MAC CWmin/max 15/1023, retry 7/7, queue 10; propagation = ConstantSpeedPropagation, path loss = FreeSpacePathLoss, obstacleLoss = "" (explicitly documented "None — not supported by MOSAIC yet", Config/README.md:239). Ad-hoc topocast, IPv4 broadcast UDP. Two documented deviations: urban_7_9 scenarios miss thermalNoise setting; docker scenarios use randomSeed 168534930 vs 268965854 in simulation/mosaic scenarios (Config/README.md:295-308).

TRAFFIC SCENARIO: InTAS (Ingolstadt Traffic Scenario, Silas Lobo, GPL-3.0) — a real-city 24h SUMO scenario of Ingolstadt, Germany (center 48.766666/11.433333). Per scenario dir: ingolstadt.net.xml 16.9MB (4,690 junctions, 196 tlLogic blocks, ~23.6k edge ids incl. internal; UTM zone 32; conv boundary ~13.6 x 11.1 km), 22 calibrated route files InTAS_001..022.rou.xml (~33-55MB each, ~910MB total per scenario) each vehicle carrying a routeDistribution with empirical route probabilities, ped.rou.xml pedestrians (SUMO striping model, stripe-width 0.55, jamtime 30), BusRoutes.flow.xml bus flows + BusStations.add.xml, InTAS_E1.add.xml induction-loop detectors, buildings.poly.xml 5.7MB + InTAS.poly.xml 8MB building polygons, sumocfg: step-length 0.1s, 86400s, Krauss car-following, rerouting device probability 0.82/period 300s, time-to-teleport 300, parking.maneuver true (Generator/docker/scenarios/InTAS_urban_2_4_test/sumo/InTAS_full_poly.sumocfg). MOSAIC<->SUMO updateInterval = 1000 ms (Config/README.md:241-248). 8 simulation runs = 4 subsets (urban/highway x 2-4AM low-density x 7-9AM rush) x test/trainval with spatially DISJOINT bounding boxes so ML models train and test on different city regions (Config/README.md:88-148).

REALISM FEATURES IN THE CAM APP (Generator/simulation/mosaic/applications/CamApp/src/main/java/): (1) ETSI EN 302 637-2-style CAM triggering — Δpos>4m OR Δheading>4° OR Δv>0.5 m/s OR max interval 1s, min interval 500ms, 200B min payload (entities/ConfigSettings; Documentation/Eclipse MOSAIC/Application/README.md:36-46, 299-332). (2) Runtime driver profiles: each vehicle randomly AGGRESSIVE 10% / NORMAL 80% / PASSIVE 10%, applied via MOSAIC requestVehicleParametersUpdate (tau 0.5/1.0/1.5, accel 3.1/2.6/2.1, decel 5.0/4.5/4.0, speedFactor 1.1/1.0/0.9, minGap 2.0/2.5/3.0, LaneChangeMode+SpeedMode AGGRESSIVE/DEFAULT/CAUTIOUS) — etsi/VehicleCamSendingApp.java:72-88,293-304; entities/DriverProfile.java:8-10; empirical resulting speed/accel distributions per density published in Documentation/Evaluation/Results/README.md:40-73. (3) Sensor error models (util/SensorErrorModel.java): GPS position = temporally correlated Gaussian, init U(-5,5) m per axis, mu=(E0+Et-1)/2, sigma=0.03*E0 (lines 39-50); speed = relative error, factor N(0, 0.00016) (52-56); acceleration error = d(speedError)/dt (58-65); heading error = U(-20,20)° decaying exp(-0.1*v) (67-78). Noise magnitudes are transmitted in the CAM as *_noise confidence fields via userTaggedValue. (4) Pseudonym change model: first change after random 800-1500 m driven; subsequent changes require distance AND elapsed time 120-360 s; 10-digit random pseudonyms (VehicleCamSendingApp.java:172-200) — NOTE it uses wall-clock LocalDateTime.now() for the time criterion (lines 59,175,192), a sim-time bug. (5) Buses carry no V2X app (mapping: bus prototype has no applications); 45 vehicle prototypes (random_001-022/default_001-022 matching InTAS vTypes + bus) all weight 1.0 running etsi.VehicleCamSendingApp (Config/README.md:157-173).

ATTACKS = OFFLINE POST-PROCESSING (Generator/attackGenerator/attackGenerator.py; Documentation/Post-Processing/Attack Generator/README.md): 20% of vehicles become attackers; 15 attacks — constant/randomPositionOffset (±20-70m), positionMirroring (needs SUMO road-edge), constant/randomSpeedOffset (±1-7 m/s), zeroSpeedReport, suddenConstantSpeed, reversedHeading, feignedBraking (2-4x negated accel), accelerationMultiplication, timeDelayAttack (2-4s), dosAttack (2-4 duplicates), trafficCongestionSybil (4-6 phantom vehicles ±2-3m lateral/±5-6m longitudinal), suddenStop, dataReplay (400m radius, 5s window); plus mixAll/mixThree modes. CONDITIONAL ground-truth labeling: attacker=1 only when the manipulation has practical effect (e.g. reversedHeading only if moving; feignedBraking only if accel>0.25 m/s2) — README:233-253. Data enrichment adds sender distance_to_road_edge via SUMO/TraCI (enrichMsgsWithFutherInfo/enrichMsgs.py). Record schema: rcvTime/sendTime (ns), sender_id, sender_alias (pseudonym), messageID, attacker flag, sender+receiver blocks with pos/spd/acl/hed + *_noise + driversProfile + distance_to_road_edge (Documentation/README.md:115-174). Splits 50/10/40 train/val/test by timestamp + disjoint areas (Getting Started/README.md:88-108).

BUNDLED MBD BASELINE: CaTCH (Kamel et al. WCNC 2019) reimplementation with 9 uncertainty-aware plausibility/consistency checks producing confidence factors [0,1] (range/position/speed plausibility; position/speed/position-speed/position-heading consistency; intersection; sudden appearance) plus binary legacy variants, 14 Optuna-tuned thresholds; complete published per-attack/per-density F1 tables and VeReMi-Extension comparison (Documentation/Evaluation/CaTCH-MBD System/README.md; Documentation/Evaluation/Results/README.md:95-295 — e.g. urban-low F1: randomPositionOffset 0.940, zeroSpeedReport 0.907, but timeDelay 0.062, feignedBraking 0.027, sybil 0.259 — lots of headroom).

HOW OUR REPO USES IT TODAY: (1) ADR docs/adr/0001-stack-and-approach.md:9-24 — NextGen+MOSAIC chosen as the base stack (Apache-2.0 licensing, active maintenance, federation seam) over F2MD/Veins and Artery. (2) scms-sim/scenarios/gen_scenario.py:29 (NEXTGEN path), :39-42 (REG intas_urban_low/rush + intas_highway_low/rush = InTAS_*_test variants), :83-98 (copies mapping/application/output + scenario_config from Generator/simulation/mosaic/scenarios, directory-junctions the ~910MB sumo/routes, copies InTAS.db routing database from the docker variant), :102-111 (FORCES sns:true, omnetpp:false — discards NextGen's 802.11p/INET radio), :113-125 (replaces etsi.VehicleCamSendingApp with org.scms.app.ScmsBeaconApp on all 45 prototypes, drops RSU/TL/server units), :140-145 (overwrites EVERY prototype with uniform SCMS_VEH_* accel/decel/length/maxSpeed/minGap/sigma/tau), :151-161 (SUMO --scale density injection), :163-170 (SCMS_SIM_STEP override of the 1000ms updateInterval). (3) scms-sim/scenarios/make_scms_intas.ps1:1-47 — older standalone equivalent (omnetpp->sns regex swap at :33-36). (4) run.ps1:8-18 and gui/server.py:46-52,84-86,301-303 expose the 4 intas_* scenarios in the CLI/GUI. (5) src/scms_sim_ref/datagen/campaign.py:49 samples intas_urban_low/intas_highway_low in randomized dataset campaigns. (6) DATASHEET.md:20 positions our MA-perspective dataset as complementary to VeReMi/VeReMi-NextGen per-vehicle corpora. (7) NO code anywhere in src/ or tools/ reads the VeReMi JSON dataset format, downloads Zenodo data, or benchmarks against CaTCH (grep for veremi/rcvTime/sender_alias: only campaign.py scenario keys match). tools/verify_data.py has no veremi reference. The mock_pipeline's attack catalog (src/scms_sim_ref/mock_pipeline/run.py:53-60: ConstPos, ConstPosOffset, RandomPos, ConstSpeedOffset, RandomSpeed, ReversedHeading, DataReplay, Sybil, DoS, DelayedMessages...) conceptually mirrors the VeReMi taxonomy but shares no code/data. Our ScmsBeaconApp independently implements ETSI EN 302 637-2 CAM trigger rules (scms-sim/mosaic-apps/scms-app/src/main/java/org/scms/app/ScmsBeaconApp.java:140) but contains none of NextGen's SensorErrorModel/GaussMarkovNoise/DriverProfile code (grep: 0 matches in scms-sim/mosaic-apps).
gaps: RADIO DOWNGRADE: our InTAS runs force MOSAIC's SNS simple-network simulator and disable the OMNeT++/INET 802.11p federate NextGen ships (gen_scenario.py:106-107, make_scms_intas.ps1:33-36). We therefore have no CSMA/CA MAC contention, no SNIR-based reception, no hidden-terminal or channel-congestion effects, no per-packet capture behavior — the single largest V2X network-realism gap vs both a real city and the upstream dataset. The full omnetpp.ini parameter set (5.9GHz/10MHz/6Mbps/20mW/-81dBm/4dB SNIR) sits unused in the vendored scenarios.

NO OBSTACLE/BUILDING LOSS ANYWHERE: even NextGen's own radio uses FreeSpacePathLoss + ConstantSpeedPropagation with obstacleLoss explicitly empty (omnetpp.ini; Config/README.md:239), despite buildings.poly.xml (5.7MB) being present per scenario. Urban NLOS shadowing — dominant in a real city — is unmodeled upstream and in our SNS path; this is where we can exceed the SOTA reference, not just match it.

DRIVER HETEROGENEITY DESTROYED IN OUR PIPELINE: NextGen assigns per-vehicle profiles (10% aggressive / 80% normal / 10% passive, distinct tau/accel/decel/speedFactor/minGap/laneChange/speedMode) at runtime inside VehicleCamSendingApp, which we replace with ScmsBeaconApp; gen_scenario.py:140-145 then overwrites all 45 InTAS prototypes with a single uniform SCMS_VEH_* parameter set. Our InTAS traffic is behaviorally homogeneous while the upstream reference (and reality) is not.

1 Hz KINEMATIC SAMPLING: MOSAIC<->SUMO updateInterval is 1000 ms by default (sumo_config.json) although SUMO steps at 0.1 s, capping app-visible dynamics and ETSI trigger fidelity at 1 Hz; our SCMS_SIM_STEP override exists (gen_scenario.py:163-170) but is opt-in and off by default.

NO SENSOR-ERROR MODEL IN OUR BEACONS: NextGen's temporally-correlated GPS error, relative speed error, derived acceleration error, speed-dependent heading error, and the transmitted *_noise confidence fields (SensorErrorModel.java) have no counterpart in ScmsBeaconApp — our MOSAIC-path CAMs are noiselessly perfect, unlike real GNSS/CAN data, and cannot support uncertainty-aware detectors (CaTCH-class).

NO BENCHMARK LINKAGE: we neither run the bundled CaTCH MBD system (Generator/MBD_systems/) against our datasets nor evaluate our detectors on the published VeReMi-NextGen data; the published per-attack F1 tables (Results/README.md:95-295) are an unused calibration/comparison baseline. Our dataset schema is not exportable to the VeReMi JSON record format, so no external comparability.

UNCONDITIONAL ATTACK LABELING RISK: NextGen labels attacker=1 only when manipulation has practical effect (e.g. zeroSpeed only if actually moving; feignedBraking only if accelerating — Attack Generator/README.md:233-253); if our datagen labels every attacker message unconditionally, our ground truth is noisier than the reference standard.

PARTIAL SCENARIO USE: only the 4 *_test InTAS variants are registered (gen_scenario.py:39-42); the spatially disjoint *_trainval variants and NextGen's leakage-aware spatial/temporal split methodology are unused; 24h demand is truncated to 300 s defaults, so we never exercise demand transitions (night->rush ramps).

VRU/BUS REALISM DROPPED: InTAS ships pedestrians (ped.rou.xml, striping model) and bus flows with stops, and NextGen deliberately keeps buses V2X-silent; gen_scenario.py strips all non-vehicle units and our mapping ignores ped/bus route content beyond SUMO's simulation of them — no VRU beacons or heterogeneous station types on the MOSAIC path.

PSEUDONYM MODEL DIVERGENCE + UPSTREAM BUG: NextGen's privacy-realistic pseudonym change (800-1500 m + 120-360 s) uses wall-clock LocalDateTime.now() (VehicleCamSendingApp.java:59,175,189-197) — non-reproducible and wrong at sim speed; if we adopt the model, it must be re-based on simulation time.

SUBMODULE PIN OPACITY: the submodule is one squashed commit ('add scenarios', acda994) with vendored MOSAIC 25.0 jars while the docker/README claim 25.2; version drift between our C:/Users/Administrator/tools MOSAIC 25.2 toolchain and the vendored tree is unaudited.
opportunities: Re-enable the 802.11p radio for flagship runs: add an omnetpp variant to gen_scenario.py (keep omnetpp:true, reuse the vendored scenarios' omnetpp/omnetpp.ini verbatim). On Windows, easiest via NextGen's docker images (ghcr.io/vs-uulm/veremi-nextgen:recreation for exact versions, :latest for current; Getting Started/README.md:7-49) since OMNeT++ isn't in C:/Users/Administrator/tools; the omnet_installer.sh path in Generator/simulation/mosaic/bin/fed/omnetpp is the non-docker route. Hook point: gen_scenario.py:102-111 federate block.

Calibrate SNS against the INET ground truth: derive SCMS_RADIO_RANGE/SCMS_RADIO_LOSS (mapgen.write_sns_config, gen_scenario.py:149) from the omnetpp.ini physics (20 mW, -81 dBm, free-space => deterministic max range; add distance-dependent loss to approximate SNIR behavior), and validate by running the same scenario under both radios and comparing reception-distance/PDR curves.

Add building-aware shadowing neither stack has: parse the per-scenario buildings.poly.xml/InTAS.poly.xml to compute LOS/NLOS per tx-rx pair (GEMV2-style or simple wall-count attenuation) inside our SNS-side loss model — this leapfrogs the upstream SOTA which explicitly lacks obstacle loss.

Port driver heterogeneity into ScmsBeaconApp: reimplement applyDriverProfile() (VehicleCamSendingApp.java:293-304 uses the public MOSAIC requestVehicleParametersUpdate API; profile constants in DriverProfile.java:8-10, mix 10/80/10 at VehicleCamSendingApp.java:72-88) and make gen_scenario.py:140-145 apply SCMS_VEH_* as a per-prototype jittered distribution instead of one uniform set; validate against the published profile speed/accel distributions (Results/README.md:40-73).

Port SensorErrorModel (85 lines, EPL-2.0-compatible) into ScmsBeaconApp and carry pos/spd/acl/hed noise-confidence fields in SignedCam — prerequisite for uncertainty-aware (CaTCH-class) detection and for realistic GNSS error in the emitted dataset; fix the wall-clock pseudonym-timer bug when porting the pseudonym model (use getOs().getSimulationTime()).

Build a VeReMi-format exporter + benchmark harness: (a) map our per-receiver records to the NextGen JSON schema (Documentation/README.md:115-174) so Generator/MBD_systems/main.py (CaTCH) runs unmodified over our data; (b) run our detectors over downloaded VeReMi-NextGen subsets (Zenodo 19665762); compare to the published F1 tables (Results/README.md:95-295) — the weak upstream results on timeDelay (F1 0.06), feignedBraking (0.03), sybil (0.14-0.26) are publishable targets.

Adopt conditional attack labeling rules (Attack Generator/README.md:233-253) in src/scms_sim_ref datagen so ground truth matches the reference standard (label attacker=1 only when manipulation is behaviorally observable).

Use InTAS's own instrumentation for traffic-realism validation: InTAS_E1.add.xml induction loops + summary/statistic/tripinfo outputs are already in every copied scenario — compare simulated detector counts across --scale settings to the InTAS-calibrated baseline as an automated realism regression test.

Register the *_trainval InTAS variants (spatially disjoint areas, Config/README.md:99-116) in gen_scenario.py REG and reuse NextGen's 50/10/40 time+space split discipline in our campaign/leakage_linter pipeline for leakage-free ML splits.

Longer-horizon runs: expose durations beyond 300 s (the underlying demand is a full 24h with distinct 2-4AM and 7-9AM regimes) to capture density transitions; the time-window mechanics are already parameterized via scenario_config duration (gen_scenario.py:108).

Mine attackGenerator.py's parameterizations (offset ranges, phantom-vehicle geometry, replay radius/window) to align mock_pipeline attack magnitudes (run.py:53-60 catalog) with the published reference, making cross-corpus detector results comparable.
notes: Licensing: repo top-level LICENSE + THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md; NextGen's own code is permissive (our ADR cites Apache-2.0), but InTAS SUMO assets are GPL-3.0 (header in InTAS_full_poly.sumocfg) and CamApp carries an EPL-2.0 Fraunhofer FOKUS header (VehicleCamSendingApp.java:1-14) — our make_scms_intas.ps1 already git-ignores generated scenarios for this reason (comment lines 5-7); any ported Java (SensorErrorModel/DriverProfile) inherits EPL-2.0, fine alongside Apache-2.0 but keep attribution. Scale facts for planning: each of the 8 scenario dirs carries its own ~910MB routes copy (submodule ~16GB total, routes junctioned into generated scenarios, never copied); route files use per-vehicle routeDistribution alternatives so SUMO's rerouting device (prob 0.82) picks among calibrated routes at runtime. The vendored Generator/simulation/mosaic tree bundles MOSAIC 25.0 jars whereas docker builds 25.2 — our toolchain at C:/Users/Administrator/tools/mosaic is 25.2, matching the docker path. Local submodule working tree is currently clean (parent 'm' flag appears to be stale/junction-related). InTAS net metrics measured directly: 4,690 junctions, 196 tlLogic, ~23.6k edge ids (incl. internal), UTM32N, netOffset -464198.88,-4952821.58 (matches scenario_config cartesian offset).
